rules.name: Remove the CORBA dependency (org.omg.*) instead of retrofitting it
rules.description: Java SE 11 removes the java.corba module (JEP 320). The org.omg.CORBA, org.omg.CosNaming, org.omg.PortableServer and related packages no longer exist in the JDK runtime image, so any source referencing org.omg.* fails to compile on JDK 11. JEP 320 states there will be no standalone CORBA unless third parties take over maintenance, and that RMI-IIOP has no standalone version at all. In JADE the whole CORBA surface is one component: the idlj-generated IDL stub package FIPA (42 files generated from src/fipa.idl) plus the single IIOP message transport jade/mtp/iiop/MessageTransportProtocol.java, which is the only file in the workspace that imports package FIPA. The knowledge graph shows zero incoming edges into that component from the other 972 workspace files, and the default MTP selected by jade/core/ProfileImpl.java is jade.mtp.http.MessageTransportProtocol. The dependency is therefore deleted, not re-supplied from an external jar. Because the fix is deletion of a whole component, the rule flags two constructs: (1) a source reference to a removed org.omg.* type, and (2) membership of the generated FIPA stub package itself, which exists only to carry those references. Five of the 42 generated files carry no org.omg reference of their own (AgentID, DateTime, Envelope, FipaMessage, ReceivedObject) yet cannot survive the deletion of their siblings: FipaMessage declares a FIPA.Envelope[] field and ReceivedObject a FIPA.DateTime field. Construct (2) is what makes the component complete in the flag index, and therefore complete in the shard plan.

It cannot be split into independently verifiable parallel shards, which is why it is classified signature and planned as a single coherent shard.

component_completeness.note: Pattern 2 (package FIPA;) matches exactly 42 files, every one of them under src/jade/src/FIPA/, and zero files anywhere else in the 1015-file workspace. It exists because plan_shards.py derives editable_files from flagged files plus their one-hop dependents; with the org.omg patterns alone, FIPA/DateTime.java and FIPA/ReceivedObject.java fell outside the shard entirely and FIPA/FipaMessage.java landed in read_only_context, so the shard could not delete the component it was planned for and FipaMessage.java would have been left referencing a deleted FIPA.Envelope.

rules.name: Anonymous TLS cipher suites are disabled by default in JDK 11
rules.description: In JDK 11 the java.security property jdk.tls.disabledAlgorithms has the default value 'SSLv3, TLSv1, TLSv1.1, DTLSv1.0, RC4, DES, MD5withRSA, DH keySize < 1024, EC keySize < 224, 3DES_EDE_CBC, anon, NULL, ECDH, include jdk.disabled.namedCurves'. The 'anon' entry disables every anonymous key-exchange cipher suite (DH_anon, ECDH_anon), and the JSSE guide states these algorithms will not be negotiated for TLS/DTLS connections even if they are enabled explicitly by an application. JADE hard-codes anonymous suites in two places, so an SSLServerSocket configured with them raises an SSLHandshakeException at runtime on JDK 11 instead of completing an unauthenticated handshake.

blast_class_evidence.reason: Both occurrences are String literals inside a String[] initializer. The declared types (List, String[]) and every method signature around them stay identical, so the edit never leaves the enclosing declaration.

blast_class_evidence.escalation_condition: If the accepted fix replaces anonymous suites with authenticated ones, the JICP peer needs key material and the change stops being body-local; that is an architectural decision reserved for the user, and the recipe must stop and report it rather than invent a keystore.

rules.verification_hint: No .java file in the workspace matches (?:TLS|SSL)_(?:DH|ECDH)_anon_ any more, or every remaining match is proven unreachable. A JICP-S handshake between two JADE containers on JDK 11 completes without SSLHandshakeException, and all four consumers still PASS.

withdrawn_rules.reason: Withdrawn on evidence, not deferred. The entire behaviour change is one comma in a debug GUI timestamp: JRE/COMPAT rendered "11/14/23 10:13 PM" and CLDR renders "11/14/23, 10:13 PM". The proposed fix hard-codes the English COMPAT pattern, which would stop the tools honouring the user's locale -- a regression for non-English operators, and a worse outcome than the comma it avoids. No site is broken by the CLDR default.
